newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 4.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 4:
WASHINGTON - Vice President Al Gore asserted he broke no laws but said he would no longer make telephone solicitations from his office because the calls had aroused such concern.

WASHINGTON - Gore discovered that it's far easier to play the role of loyal understudy to President Clinton than face questions about his role in raising millions of dollars in political contributions.
WASHINGTON - A program to streamline the process for granting U.S. citizenship to immigrants came under heavy White House presssure to speed up its procedures.
WASHINGTON - Teenagers see less of a drug problem in their schools than their parents do.
WASHINGTON - Former CIA case officer Harold James Nicholson pleaded guilty to spying for Russia and agreed to tell investigators what secrets he gave away.

DENVER - The lawyer for accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh charged that a Dallas newspaper has stolen virtually the entire defense file in the case and said he may ask for a 90-day delay in the trial.
SEOUL, SOUTH KOREA - Some in South Korea fear the chaos and cost of uniting their prosperous nation with North Korea, one of the world's msot impoverished.
